title: Age of New Worlds - turn-based 4X strategy game
author: ernestwisniewski
selftext:
I’ve been working on hobby project - Age of New Worlds, a turn-based 4X strategy game. AI is part of the workflow, but I'm trying to use it more as a tool for iteration than as a "generate everything and ship it" button.

I also keep a devlog ([https://ernest.dev](https://ernest.dev)) where I describe the more technical side of the project, architecture decisions, experiments, refactors, engine work, and why I choose one approach over another.

Most of the current visual assets started as images generated with ChatGPT. After that I manually cleaned them up, combined elements, adjusted composition, removed artifacts, changed colors, and generally processed them in Photopea until they worked reasonably well inside the game.

I treat these graphics more as a visual direction / prototype than a final locked art style.

The longer-term plan is actually to replace many of them with 3D scenes built in Godot and rendered back into 2D assets. I’m currently experimenting with recreating the game’s maps, terrain, cities and other elements in Godot, while keeping the existing 2D version of the game alive.

To make future replacement easier, the project also contains an SVG template for every asset, so swapping generated graphics for redesigned or rendered versions should not require rebuilding the whole UI around them.

AI assistance on this project goes beyond graphics too. I’ve been using Codex mostly for:

* code reviews,
* discussing architecture and possible approaches,
* finding problems during larger refactors,
* maintaining and updating project documentation.

I still make the architectural and design decisions myself, but having something that can inspect a large codebase and challenge an implementation has been particularly useful for a solo project.

What I find interesting is that the role of AI in the project keeps changing. At first it was mainly helping me create assets I simply couldn’t create myself. Now some of those assets are becoming references for a more traditional 3D pipeline.

So instead of:

**AI image → final game asset**

it is increasingly becoming:

**AI concept → manual editing → prototype → 3D recreation in Godot → rendered 2D asset**
